raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I've been farming these 10 mu for most of my life, and my father farmed it before me. Wheat then maize, wheat then maize — that's what this land does.

**Winter wheat (already in the ground since last October, about 10 mu)**

I planted "Jimai 22" again this October past — it's what the seed shop had and what my neighbors use. Good variety for our area, disease-resistant enough. I saved a bit from last year but bought new seed too, maybe 15 kg/mu at around 5 yuan/kg. Before sowing I spread a compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind, about 40 kg/mu. That's my base fertilizer for the whole wheat season for P and K.

Now it's spring, the wheat is greening up. Around the jointing stage (late March, early April) I'll topdress urea — probably 20 kg/mu. The extension technician came through the village a few years back and said 15 kg was enough, but I've always done a little more and my yield is fine, so I keep doing what works. If the wheat looks pale I might push to 25.

Irrigation — I'll water at greening, jointing, and heading. Three times usually does it. If spring is dry I'll add one at grain filling. Well water costs me around 40-50 yuan each time for my 10 mu with the electric pump. Not cheap, but you can't skip it or the yield falls off.

Pests and weeds — I'll spray a herbicide once in early spring for broadleaf weeds, and watch for aphids at heading. Usually one insecticide pass is enough. My son helps me with the sprayer when he's home from the city.

I expect around 420 kg/mu. Last year I got 440, year before was 400 because spring was dry. That's a realistic number for my land.

**Summer maize (planted right after wheat harvest in mid-June, same 10 mu)**

Tight window after wheat comes off around June 10th. I hire the combine, straw gets chopped and left on the field, then I hire a no-till planter to put the maize in. Same day or next day. No time for plowing in our system.

Seed: a hybrid, probably "Zhengdan 958" or whatever the shop recommends that year. About 3 kg/mu, costs me around 40-50 yuan/mu for seed.

Fertilizer for maize: I put down compound at planting — about 30 kg/mu of the 15-15-15 — and then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage (jointing), maybe 20 kg/mu. Total N around 13-14 kg/mu if I add it up, but honestly I think in bags, not kilograms of N. Maize on this land has always done well — the summer rain helps a lot.

Irrigation for maize depends on the rains. Usually I water once at planting to get germination, and once more at tasseling if July is dry. Sometimes I don't irrigate maize at all if the rain comes right. Two times at most.

Pesticide: one herbicide pass after planting, maybe one insecticide if armyworm shows up. My eyes aren't what they were, so my son or I walk the field weekly.

Yield expectation: around 500 kg/mu. Our village gets good maize — 450 to 550 is normal.

**Why I farm this way**

I'm 65. I've tried a few things over the years — different varieties, different fertilizer amounts — and I've settled on what gives me steady yield without gambling. My kids help with the heavy work but they have their own jobs in the city. My wife and I do most of it with machinery hired for planting and harvest. The land feeds us and gives us some cash. At my age I'm not going to chase the last 10% of yield by spending another 500 yuan on inputs. Steady is what I want.
